entries.title: Data Display/VirtualList
entries.name: VirtualList
entries.description: VirtualList is a fast, windowed, variable-height list that renders only the rows near the viewport (plus a render-ahead buffer). One source runs on web and React Native by riding ScrollArea and driving windowing off `onScrollPositionChange`; row heights are measured via `onLayout` and fed to a per-type running-average size model, so no exact `estimatedItemSize` is required. Mirrors the familiar FlatList / FlashList surface (`data`, `renderItem`, `keyExtractor`, `getItemType`, `onEndReached`, `ListHeaderComponent`/`ListFooterComponent`/`ListEmptyComponent`/`ItemSeparatorComponent`) plus an imperative handle (`scrollToIndex` / `scrollToOffset` / `scrollToEnd`). Set `keepMounted` when rows own state that must survive scrolling out of view — a bounded LRU warm pool (`keepMounted={40}`) or everything ever mounted (`keepMounted`).

stories.name: Basic
stories.description: 10,000 fixed-height rows — scroll freely; only ~a dozen nodes are mounted.

stories.name: VariableHeights
stories.description: Rows of differing heights — measured on mount and estimated by running average.

stories.description: Imperative scrolling via the ref handle.

stories.name: InfiniteScroll
stories.description: `onEndReached` drives infinite loading — rows append as you near the bottom.

stories.name: KeepMounted
stories.description: `keepMounted` — rows keep their own state after scrolling out of view. Both lists render the same stateful row (a per-row counter). Bump a few counters near the top, scroll to the bottom, then scroll back: the plain list unmounted those rows and their counts are back to 0, while the `keepMounted` list kept them in the tree. A number bounds the pool — the least-recently-visible rows are evicted first — so memory stays bounded on a long list.

stories.name: MountEverything
stories.description: `keepMounted="all"` — windowing off entirely. Every row in `data` is mounted from the first commit, whether or not it has ever been on screen, so find-in-page reaches every row and nothing measures late. This gives up what virtualization buys you — mount cost is O(data) — so it is for lists of a size you would have `.map()`ed anyway. The counter shows how many rows are really in the tree; compare it with the windowed list beside it.

entries.description: A data-driven Skia audio visualizer. An external driver only ever pushes new TARGET states (a row of 0..1 levels) via the imperative ref handle (`ref.push(levels)`) or a `target` SharedValue — the easing TRANSITION between states lives inside the component, paced on the display clock (`requestAnimationFrame`), double-buffered, off the React render path, and self-suspending when idle. `useDerivedValue` worklets build the `SkPath`s so the per-frame paint never re-renders React. Filled with a Skia gradient and optional glow. Identical on native and web (web needs `<GraphicsProvider>` + CanvasKit). Reduced-motion snaps to each target. The stories below drive it with a synthetic ticker.

stories.name: Default
stories.description: The default mirrored waveform, driven by a smooth travelling sine.

stories.name: Bars
stories.description: Vertical bars filled with a linear gradient.

stories.name: Line
stories.description: A stroked line tracing the level at each point.

stories.name: Dots
stories.description: A dot per bar, sized by level.

stories.name: Wave
stories.description: A filled, mirrored envelope (smooth waveform area) with a glow.

stories.name: Radial
stories.description: Spokes radiating from the centre, with a sweep gradient pivoting on the centre.

stories.name: BurstyTicks
stories.description: The headline story: a BURSTY, irregular data source (jittery delivery + occasional stalls) — yet the on-screen motion stays smooth because the easing transition is paced on the display clock, not the data clock.

stories.name: Smoothed
stories.description: Jumpy per-bar noise, tamed by heavy smoothing — the transition does the work.

stories.name: Glow
stories.description: A soft glow behind a sweep-gradient mirror waveform.

stories.name: Neon
stories.description: A neon look: a crisp shape with a separate, brightly-tinted blurred halo (`glowColor`).

stories.name: VuMeter
stories.description: VU-meter feel: a snappy attack (peaks pop) with a slow release (a gentle decay tail).

stories.name: HorizontalGradient
stories.description: A horizontal gradient running left→right across the bars instead of top→bottom.

stories.name: RestingFloor
stories.description: A resting baseline (`floor`) so the visualizer always shows a lively bed of bars.

stories.name: Gain
stories.description: Boosted sensitivity (`gain`) — quiet input pushed up toward the ceiling and clamped.

stories.name: Tinted
stories.description: A tinted background with a translucent shape (`backgroundColor` + `opacity`).

stories.name: TargetSharedValue
stories.description: Driven by a `target` SharedValue instead of the ref handle: write `target.value = levels` from any JS-thread loop and the visualizer eases toward it. While a `target` is set the display loop runs continuously (it can't listen to SV writes portably), so prefer the ref `push()` for the self-suspending path.

entries.title: Graphics/Core/GraphicsProvider
entries.name: GraphicsProvider
entries.description: Initializes the Skia graphics runtime. On native it's a pass-through (Skia is linked into the app); on web it loads the CanvasKit WASM blob and renders `fallback` until it's ready, exposing the state via `useGraphicsReady()`. Wrap your app once, near the root — every graphics component must render beneath it on web. (Storybook already wraps all stories in one, so this is just for illustration.)

entries.title: Graphics/Effects/EffectView
entries.name: EffectView
entries.description: A drop-in `<div>` replacement that paints a stack of Skia effects onto itself. Pass `effects` as one array of `{ effect, ...props }` descriptors — frame paints (`fill`, `border`, `glow`, `shadow`) and component-backed effects (`dottedGrid`, `checkerboard`, `noise`, `image`, `blurredImage`). Array order is stacking order; you pass data, never a component. Geometry (corner radius and size) is read off the element's own `style`. All layers paint into at most two shared Skia canvases (one behind the content, one in front), clipped with a Skia `Group`. A native counterpart (`View.native.tsx`) wraps a React Native `View`.

stories.name: Playground
stories.description: A gradient border offset outward from the box, with a soft drop shadow under it.

stories.name: SweepBorder
stories.description: A conic (sweep) gradient border hugging the box edge.

stories.name: GradientFill
stories.description: A Skia gradient `fill` painted into the rounded box, plus a soft glow.

stories.name: Layers
stories.description: Stacking component-backed effects: a `noise` texture and a `dottedGrid` filling the box (clipped to its rounded corners), under a gradient border. One array, bottom-to-top — no components passed in.

stories.name: Combined
stories.description: Everything at once: gradient fill, offset gradient border, outer + inner shadows.

entries.title: Graphics/Effects/ShadowView
entries.name: ShadowView
entries.description: A drop-in View that renders a drop shadow from React Native's `shadow*` inputs (`shadowColor`, `shadowOffset`, `shadowRadius`, `shadowOpacity`) consistently across platforms. On web it maps to a CSS `box-shadow`; the native counterpart (`ShadowView.native.tsx`) paints the shadow with Skia via `EffectView`, so it works on Android too — which ignores RN's `shadow*` style props natively. Pass the shadow as props or in `style`; on native the props are stripped from the underlying View so iOS doesn't double up. Geometry (size + corner radius) is read off `style`.

stories.name: Default
stories.description: A soft drop shadow under the card.

stories.name: Elevated
stories.description: A tight, dark shadow offset down-right.

stories.name: Inner
stories.description: An inset shadow painted inside the box.

stories.name: Colored
stories.description: A colored glow-like shadow.

entries.title: Icons/Icon
entries.name: Icon
entries.description: The icon package wraps Tabler icons with lazy-loaded web and native entry points. Use `Icon` with a registry name, or import a generated `Icon*` component directly.

name.description: Registry name for the icon to render.

entries.title: Camera/Camera
entries.name: Camera
entries.description: Camera controls the map viewport — both declaratively (via props such as `center`, `zoom`, `bearing`, `pitch`, `padding`, and `initialViewState`) and imperatively (via a `CameraRef` exposing `flyTo`, `easeTo`, `jumpTo`, `fitBounds`, and `zoomTo`). Coordinates are `[longitude, latitude]`; bounds are `[west, south, east, north]`.

stories.name: Declarative
stories.description: Set the starting viewport once, declaratively, via `initialViewState`.

stories.name: CenterAndZoom
stories.description: Drive center + zoom directly as controlled props.

stories.name: BearingAndPitch
stories.description: A tilted, rotated 3D-style view via `bearing` + `pitch`.

stories.name: Padding
stories.description: `padding` insets the focal point so the center sits off to one side — handy when a sidebar or panel overlaps part of the map.

stories.name: FitBoundsOnMount
stories.description: Fit a bounding box on mount by passing `bounds` to `initialViewState`.

stories.name: Constraints
stories.description: Constrain interaction with `minZoom` / `maxZoom` / `maxBounds`.

stories.name: ImperativeControls
stories.description: Imperative control via a `CameraRef`. The on-screen buttons call `flyTo`, `easeTo`, `jumpTo`, `fitBounds`, and `zoomTo` to move the camera between cities.

entries.title: Map/Interactivity
entries.name: Interactivity
entries.description: The map surfaces user interaction through event callbacks. `onPress` fires for taps/clicks with the `lngLat`, screen `point`, and any hit `features`; `onRegionDidChange` fires when the viewport settles, reporting the new center, zoom, bearing, pitch, and bounds. A `MapRef` adds imperative queries such as `getCenter`, `getZoom`, and `queryRenderedFeatures`.

stories.name: OnPress
stories.description: Record where the user clicks and show the coordinates in an overlay panel.

stories.name: OnRegionDidChange
stories.description: Track the live viewport as the user pans and zooms.

stories.name: ImperativeRef
stories.description: Use a ref to imperatively read the viewport on demand.

entries.title: Layers/Background Layer
entries.name: Background Layer
entries.description: `BackgroundLayer` paints a solid color (or pattern) across the entire map viewport. It is the one layer with **no source** — it has nothing to reference and is added as a direct child of `<Map>`. Drawn first it acts as a backdrop beneath other layers; with a translucent `backgroundColor` it tints whatever sits below it.

stories.name: SolidColor
stories.description: A solid background color filling the map — no tiles, just a flat backdrop.

stories.name: TranslucentTint
stories.description: A semi-transparent tint laid over the basemap — useful for dimming or warming the map without hiding it.

entries.title: Layers/Circle Layer
entries.name: Circle Layer
entries.description: `CircleLayer` renders point features as filled circles. Each paint property — `circleRadius`, `circleColor`, `circleStrokeColor`, `circleOpacity` — accepts a constant or a data-driven expression, so circles can be styled per-feature or by zoom. It must live inside a source and reference it via `source`.

stories.name: Basic
stories.description: A single constant style applied to every point.

stories.name: DataDriven
stories.description: Data-driven: both radius and color are interpolated from each city's `population`, so larger cities render as bigger, darker circles.

stories.name: Stroked
stories.description: Stroked circles: a white halo plus a colored ring around each point.

stories.name: StylingVariations
stories.description: Styling variations: a soft, blurred glow with a translucent fill and a thin tinted stroke — useful for ambient / heatmap-like point markers.

entries.title: Layers/Fill Extrusion Layer
entries.name: Fill Extrusion Layer
entries.description: `FillExtrusionLayer` renders polygons as extruded 3D volumes. `fillExtrusionHeight` (and optional `fillExtrusionBase`) drive each shape's vertical extent — typically from a data-driven `height` property — and are best viewed with a tilted `Camera` (`pitch`/`bearing`). Shading responds to the map's `<Light>`. It must live inside a source and reference it via `source`.

stories.name: Buildings3D
stories.description: 3D buildings extruded by each footprint's `height` property, viewed at a tilt.

stories.name: ColoredByHeight
stories.description: Height-driven color ramp: shorter buildings are light, taller ones deepen to blue.

stories.name: WithLight
stories.description: The same extrusions paired with a `<Light>`: a warm, low-anchored directional light shifts how the building faces are shaded.

entries.title: Layers/Fill Layer
entries.name: Fill Layer
entries.description: `FillLayer` paints the interior of `Polygon` features. `fillColor` and `fillOpacity` set the fill, `fillOutlineColor` adds a 1px crisp edge, and `fillColor` can be a data-driven expression to choropleth-shade regions by a property.

stories.name: Basic
stories.description: A single translucent fill over one polygon.

stories.name: DataDriven
stories.description: Data-driven: `fillColor` is interpolated from each region's `density`, producing a choropleth from pale to deep red.

stories.name: WithOutline
stories.description: A fill with a contrasting outline color to crisply delineate the polygon.

stories.name: StylingVariations
stories.description: Styling variations: a near-solid, high-opacity fill with antialiasing disabled for a flat, poster-like region block.

entries.title: Layers/Heatmap Layer
entries.name: Heatmap Layer
entries.description: `HeatmapLayer` renders point density as a smooth, color-graded surface. `heatmapWeight` weights individual points, `heatmapRadius` controls the blur kernel, `heatmapIntensity` scales the overall signal, and `heatmapColor` maps the `heatmap-density` ramp (0 → 1) to colors. It must live inside a source and reference it via `source`.

stories.name: Density
stories.description: A density heatmap from ~400 scattered points around Berlin.

stories.name: RadiusAndIntensity
stories.description: Larger radius and higher intensity produce a softer, hotter bloom.

stories.name: CustomColorRamp
stories.description: A custom `heatmapColor` ramp: transparent blue at low density rising through royal blue, lime and yellow to red at the hottest cores.

entries.title: Layers/Light
entries.name: Light
entries.description: `Light` configures the global illumination used to shade 3D `FillExtrusion` geometry. It takes no source and is added as a direct child of `<Map>`, affecting every extrusion layer at once. `anchor` ties the light to the `map` or the `viewport`, `position` is a radial `[r, azimuth, polar]` direction, and `color`/`intensity` set its tone and strength.

stories.name: Overhead
stories.description: Default-ish overhead light: high intensity, neutral color, anchored to the viewport.

stories.name: WarmLowAngle
stories.description: A warm, low, side-angled light — the lower polar angle and amber color cast longer, sunset-like shading across the same buildings.

stories.name: CoolDim
stories.description: A dim, cool light — low intensity with a blue tint produces flatter, moodier shading.

entries.title: Layers/Line Layer
entries.name: Line Layer
entries.description: `LineLayer` strokes `LineString` features. `lineCap` and `lineJoin` control end and corner shape, `lineDasharray` makes dashed strokes, and `lineWidth` (like every paint property) can be a constant or a zoom-driven expression for routes that thicken as you zoom in.

stories.name: Basic
stories.description: A simple constant-width stroke along the route.

stories.name: DataDriven
stories.description: Data-driven: `lineWidth` is interpolated by `zoom`, so the route is a thin hairline when zoomed out and a bold stroke when zoomed in.

stories.name: Dashed
stories.description: A dashed line — good for boundaries, planned routes, or footpaths.

stories.name: ThickRoute
stories.description: A thick, rounded route casing — bold cap and join for a smooth path.

stories.name: StylingVariations
stories.description: Styling variations: a soft, blurred glow stroke with a widened gap, layered to read like a highlighted corridor.

entries.title: Layers/Symbol Layer
entries.name: Symbol Layer
entries.description: `SymbolLayer` places text labels and/or icons at point features. `textField` (commonly an expression reading a feature property) supplies the label; `textHaloColor`/`textHaloWidth` keep it legible over any basemap; `iconImage` references a sprite registered via `<Images>`. Glyphs are loaded from the map style, so use a style that ships a `glyphs` endpoint (e.g. the Carto streets style). It must live inside a source and reference it via `source`.

stories.name: TextLabels
stories.description: Plain text labels reading each city's `name`.

stories.name: HaloLabels
stories.description: Styled labels with a white halo for legibility over busy areas, offset upward and anchored from the top.

stories.name: WithIcon
stories.description: An icon registered via `<Images>` placed at each city, with the name labelled beneath it. `iconImage` references the sprite by the key it was registered under.

entries.title: Map/MapView
entries.name: MapView
entries.description: `Map` is the cross-platform container. The same JSX renders via `maplibre-gl` on web and `@maplibre/maplibre-react-native` on native — the public props are RN-first and never leak engine types. Children (`Camera`, sources, layers, markers) configure the map through context.

mapStyle.description: MapLibre style URL or JSON style object.

stories.name: Basic
stories.description: The simplest possible map — a style and an initial camera position.

stories.name: StreetsBasemap
stories.description: A vector basemap with streets and labels (Carto Positron).

stories.name: Minimal
stories.description: Ornaments toggled off for an embedded / minimal look.

stories.name: Static
stories.description: Gestures disabled — a static, non-interactive map.

entries.title: Markers & Annotations/Callout
entries.name: Callout
entries.description: `Callout` is a speech-bubble that belongs to a marker's selected state on native (`@maplibre/maplibre-react-native`). On web it has no native marker host, so it renders as a best-effort inline bubble — here it is placed inside a `Marker` so it appears anchored on the map. Treat web rendering as a preview; the authoritative behaviour is on native.

stories.name: Basic
stories.description: A simple callout bubble with a title and content (web best-effort).

stories.name: TitleOnly
stories.description: Title-only callout — children fall back to the `title` text.

entries.title: Markers & Annotations/Layer Annotation
entries.name: Layer Annotation
entries.description: `LayerAnnotation` renders custom content at a coordinate as part of the map's layer stack (the native `MarkerView`/annotation primitive). It supports `animated` movement and an `onPress` handler. On web the children render as a positioned overlay.

stories.name: Single
stories.description: Custom content anchored at a single coordinate.

stories.name: Multiple
stories.description: A couple of layer annotations across several cities.

entries.title: Markers & Annotations/Marker
entries.name: Marker
entries.description: `Marker` renders a single React element as an overlay pinned to a geographic coordinate. On web your children become a DOM overlay positioned by `maplibre-gl`; on native the same element renders through the RN bridge. `anchor` and `offset` control which point of the element aligns with the coordinate.

stories.name: Single
stories.description: A single custom HTML pin anchored at a coordinate.

stories.name: ManyCities
stories.description: Many markers mapped from `EUROPEAN_CITIES`, one styled pin per city.

stories.name: Selectable
stories.description: A marker whose `onPress` toggles its own selected state (and color).

stories.name: AnchorAndOffset
stories.description: The same coordinate with different `anchor` / `offset` values to show alignment.

entries.title: Markers & Annotations/View Annotation
entries.name: View Annotation
entries.description: `ViewAnnotation` anchors arbitrary React content at a coordinate. Unlike `Marker` it carries `title`/`snippet` metadata and selection callbacks (`onSelect`/`onDeselect`). On web the children render as a DOM overlay positioned by the map engine.

stories.name: Single
stories.description: Custom React content anchored at a single coordinate.

stories.name: Multiple
stories.description: Several annotations at once, one per landmark city.

stories.name: TitleAndSnippet
stories.description: Using `title` / `snippet` metadata alongside the rendered content.

entries.title: Sources/GeoJSON Source
entries.name: GeoJSON Source
entries.description: `GeoJSONSource` (exported alias of `ShapeSource`) feeds inline GeoJSON — or a URL — into the map. Layers nested inside it reference it via `source` matching the source `id`, so the same data can drive circles, lines, fills, and clustered symbols. Set `cluster` to aggregate dense point sets into count bubbles.

stories.name: Points
stories.description: Point features rendered as circles, sized by data via a `CircleLayer`.

stories.name: Route
stories.description: A `LineString` route drawn with a styled `LineLayer`.

stories.name: Polygon
stories.description: A `Polygon` filled and outlined with a `FillLayer`.

stories.name: Clustering
stories.description: Clustering: 400 points aggregated into count bubbles. A `CircleLayer` (filtered to clusters) sizes and colors bubbles via a `step` expression on `point_count`, a `SymbolLayer` prints the count, and a third `CircleLayer` (filtered to non-clustered) draws the individual points.

entries.title: Sources/Image Source
entries.name: Image Source
entries.description: `ImageSource` pins a single static image to four geographic corners. Pair it with a `RasterLayer` that targets the source `id` to render the image — useful for floorplans, historical maps, or rendered overlays georeferenced onto the map.

stories.name: Overlay
stories.description: An image draped over a bounding box on the streets basemap.

entries.title: Sources/Raster Source
entries.name: Raster Source
entries.description: `RasterSource` loads slippy-map raster tiles (XYZ `tiles` or a TileJSON `url`) and pairs with a `RasterLayer` to paint them. Use it as a full basemap, or stack it semi-transparently over a vector style for an overlay.

stories.name: OSMTiles
stories.description: OpenStreetMap raster tiles as a full-screen basemap.

stories.name: SemiTransparentOverlay
stories.description: The same OSM tiles at `rasterOpacity: 0.5`, blended over the streets basemap.

entries.title: Sources/SVG Icon
entries.name: SVG Icon
entries.description: `SvgImage` registers an SVG resource as a named MapLibre image so a `SymbolLayer` can draw it as a **fixed-size icon** (`iconImage` + `iconSize`) that stays the same screen size at every zoom level — the usual pin/marker behaviour. SVG resources are rasterized to a bitmap via **react-native-svg on both web and native** (identical output on each platform); the marker is then drawn on the GPU by MapLibre, so a single icon backs thousands of markers with **no per-marker DOM or native view**. Raster resources (a `source` asset, or a non-SVG `uri`) are registered directly.

stories.name: FixedSizeIcons
stories.description: The SVG pin is drawn as a 40px icon at three cities. Zoom in/out — the pins keep their pixel size instead of scaling with the map.

stories.name: FromUrl
stories.description: The icon is loaded from a URL rather than inline markup. An `.svg` (or `data:image/svg+xml`) URL is fetched and rasterized; here we use a `data:` URL so the story runs offline, but any CORS-enabled `https://…/pin.svg` works the same way.

stories.name: DataDrivenIcons
stories.description: Several distinct icons registered at once via `SvgImages`, with each marker choosing its icon from its `category` property through a data-driven `iconImage` expression. Still a single GPU `SymbolLayer`.

stories.name: TenThousandMarkers
stories.description: 10,000 SVG-icon markers, **unclustered** — every point is its own symbol. `iconAllowOverlap`/`iconIgnorePlacement` keep them all visible (no collision thinning), which is the stress case for this many symbols.

stories.name: TenThousandDataDriven
stories.description: 10,000 markers across **three** icon types selected by `category`, unclustered. One rasterized bitmap per type, one GPU `SymbolLayer` drawing them all.

stories.name: TenThousandClustered
stories.description: The same 10,000 points, **clustered**. The source aggregates dense points into count bubbles (`cluster`); a `CircleLayer` + `SymbolLayer` render the clusters (sized/colored by `point_count`), and individual leaves fall back to the SVG pin. Zoom in to break clusters apart.

stories.name: FiftyThousandClustered
stories.description: **50,000** markers, **clustered** — the recommended way to show this many points. `supercluster` aggregates dense points into count bubbles that split apart as you zoom in, keeping the visible symbol count low at every zoom and well under MapLibre's per-bucket symbol limit.

entries.title: Map/Styles
entries.name: Styles
entries.description: The package ships nine vendored MapLibre basemap styles as JSON. Each is a complete, keyless `StyleSpecification` that you hand to the map's `mapStyle` prop. The gallery below shows the same camera under every bundled style; the final story lets you switch between them with a Storybook control.

stories.name: Voyager
stories.description: Carto Voyager — a balanced, colourful basemap.

stories.name: Positron
stories.description: Carto Positron — a light, low-contrast basemap good for overlays.

stories.name: DarkMatter
stories.description: Carto Dark Matter — a dark counterpart to Positron.

stories.name: KlokantechBasic
stories.description: Klokantech Basic — a plain street-level reference basemap.

stories.name: OsmLiberty
stories.description: OSM Liberty — a vivid OpenStreetMap-derived street style.

stories.name: OsmLibertyCustom
stories.description: A customised variant of OSM Liberty.

stories.name: YodaLight
stories.description: Yoda Light — a soft, light themed basemap.

stories.name: YodaDark
stories.description: Yoda Dark — a dark themed basemap.

stories.name: ZoomstackNight
stories.description: OS Zoomstack Night — a dark, night-oriented basemap.

stories.name: StyleSwitcher
stories.description: Switch the active basemap with the `mapStyle` select control in the Controls panel. Each option maps to one of the nine bundled styles.

entries.title: User Location/User Location
entries.name: User Location
entries.description: `UserLocation` renders the device's current position on the map. On web it adds a MapLibre `GeolocateControl` button to the top-right of the map; clicking it prompts the browser for geolocation permission and, once granted, centers on and marks your location. On native (iOS/Android) it renders the platform user-location indicator. Drop it as a child of `<Map>`.

stories.name: Default
stories.description: The default user-location indicator. On web, look for the geolocate button in the top-right corner of the map — clicking it requests browser geolocation permission. Nothing appears until permission is granted.

stories.name: HeadingAndAccuracy
stories.description: With `heading`, `accuracy`, and `animated` enabled the indicator shows a heading cone and an accuracy ring, and updates smoothly. As with the default, web users must grant geolocation permission via the top-right control before anything shows.

entries.title: User Location/Native User Location
entries.name: Native User Location
entries.description: **Native-only component.** `NativeUserLocation` renders the platform's built-in user-location indicator on iOS and Android (the native MapLibre `LocationComponent` / Core Location puck), with `mode` (`default` | `heading` | `course`) and `androidPreferredFramesPerSecond`. On web it is a deliberate no-op — it renders nothing and logs a development warning. Because Storybook runs on the web, this story produces no visible output; it exists purely as API documentation. On real devices, mount it as a child of `<Map>` to display the OS location dot.

stories.name: Documentation
stories.description: This is a documentation-only story. On web you will see the basemap but no location indicator, since `NativeUserLocation` is a no-op outside iOS/Android. Run the component on a device or simulator to see the native location puck.

entries.title: User Location/User Location Puck
entries.name: User Location Puck
entries.description: **Native-only component.** `UserLocationPuck` renders the modern MapLibre Native "location puck" on iOS and Android, with `visible`, `puckBearing` (`heading` | `course`), and `puckBearingEnabled` to control whether and how the puck points. On web it is a deliberate no-op — it renders nothing and logs a development warning. Because Storybook runs on the web, this story produces no visible output; it exists purely as API documentation. On real devices, mount it as a child of `<Map>` to show the puck.

stories.name: Documentation
stories.description: This is a documentation-only story. On web you will see the basemap but no puck, since `UserLocationPuck` is a no-op outside iOS/Android. Run the component on a device or simulator to see the native location puck.

entries.title: Media/Audio
entries.name: Audio
entries.description: A hybrid, cross-platform audio player. On web it drives the real browser `HTMLAudioElement` (+ Web Audio / MediaSession); on React Native it drives `expo-audio`.

stories.name: LockScreen
stories.description: Lock-screen / now-playing controls with a **cover preview**. Setting `lockScreen` publishes the `title`/`artist`/`album`/`artwork` to the OS: on native (`expo-audio`) it owns the iOS lock screen / Android media notification, and on web it drives the browser **MediaSession** API — so the artwork shows as the cover in the OS media controls / hardware-key UI. Play it, then check your system media controls (or lock the device on a native build).

stories.name: CustomControlBar
stories.description: Compose a custom bar from the exported parts.

controls.$expr:
<Group justify="space-between" align="center" width="100%">
        <Group gap="$xs" align="center" wrap="nowrap">
          <Audio.PlayPause />
          <Audio.Time />
        </Group>
        <Group gap="$xs" align="center" wrap="nowrap">
          <Audio.Mute />
          <Audio.PlaybackRate />
        </Group>
      </Group>

stories.name: Headless
stories.description: Headless: no transport, just the header. Drive it via `Audio.useAudio()`.

stories.name: Styles
stories.description: Per-slot style overrides.

stories.name: Themed
stories.description: Theme-driven recolor. The whole player is built on `$colorN` ramp tokens, so dropping it under a `<Theme>` recolors it with zero per-component logic — the same property that themes Button/ActionIcon. No hardcoded colors anywhere.

stories.name: LongTrack
stories.description: A full, minutes-long track — gives the scrubber real range to drag across and a meaningful elapsed/remaining readout (the short sample clips are only seconds).

stories.name: TwoPlayers
stories.description: Two players sharing ONE shared audio engine (the default singleton). Press play on one, then play on the other: the engine switches to the second track and the first pauses — there is only ever ONE `<audio>` element. Return to the first and it resumes from where you left off.

entries.title: Media/AudioPlaylist
entries.name: AudioPlaylist
entries.description: A cross-platform playlist player. Web drives an internal `HTMLAudioElement` queue; native drives the expo-audio `AudioPlaylist` (gapless). One controller contract, one kit chrome (transport + scrubber + clickable track list).

entries.title: Media/Audio Visualizer
entries.name: Audio Visualizer
entries.description: A Skia-rendered audio visualizer driven by the `@knitui/media/dsp` FFT, attached to a real `<Audio>` player. `useAudioSpectrum` taps the player's off-thread sampler (`sampleUpdate`), runs the FFT once per frame, and pushes frequency bands to `<AudioVisualizer>` — no per-frame React renders. Press play. (`@knitui/graphics`/Skia is a dev-only dependency; the shipped kit is Skia-free.)

stories.name: Player
stories.description: Real player → live frequency bars off the actual track. Press play. The track is a remote, CORS-enabled source and the player sets `crossOrigin="anonymous"`, so Web Audio is allowed to read it and the bars react to the music — the real-app pattern for visualizing remote audio. (A cross-origin source WITHOUT CORS can't be sampled: the browser taints the buffer, sampling reports unsupported, and the player just plays silently to the visualizer.)

stories.name: Glow
stories.description: A neon glow behind a crisp shape (a Skia blur), still player-driven.

stories.name: Radial
stories.description: Bars radiating from the center as spokes — pair with a sweep gradient.

stories.name: LiveMicrophone
stories.description: Live microphone → `useAudioStream` PCM → `SpectrumAnalyzer` → visualizer. Press **Start** and grant mic permission. Works on web (getUserMedia) and native (expo-audio).

stories.name: VariantsPreview
stories.description: Style preview only: every built-in variant fed by a permission-free SYNTHETIC signal (no playback). Use it to compare the visual styles; the real data path is the player/microphone stories above.

entries.title: Media/LiveAudioMeter
entries.name: LiveAudioMeter
entries.description: A live microphone level meter built on `useAudioStream`. On web it captures the mic via `getUserMedia` + a Web Audio `AnalyserNode`; on React Native it wraps `expo-audio`'s `useAudioStream` (PCM buffers decoded via `decodePcm`). Both share one platform-free contract. Requires microphone permission, granted on Start.

stories.description: Two players sharing nothing but the contract — swap the source at runtime.

stories.name: TwoPlayers
stories.description: Two players sharing ONE shared video engine (the default singleton). The single `<video>` teleports into whichever player you press play on; the other shows its poster and pauses. Returning to the first resumes from where you left off — and there is only ever ONE `<video>` element in the DOM.

stories.name: NowPlaying
stories.description: Now-playing / lock-screen controls with a **cover preview**. `nowPlaying` folds the `title`/`artist`/`artwork` into the source metadata and flips `expo-video`'s `showNowPlayingNotification` + `staysActiveInBackground`, so the OS shows a media notification with the artwork as the cover and playback keeps going in the background. Native-only — surfacing it on a device build also needs the `expo-video` config plugin's `supportsBackgroundPlayback: true`. (No-op on web; the story still renders a normal player there.)
